title: Derived sections pullback and unit-Leray pasting for geometric morphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites with terminal objects [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R$ be a commutative ring. Use sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf $R$ on each site [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their bounded-below derived categories $D^+$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be geometric morphisms [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. On constant-$R$ modules use their induced exact inverse images and right adjoints, with the canonical coefficient identifications preserving constant sections. Write $\eta_u$ for the unit of the derived adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$, for $u=f,g,fg$. Let $R\Gamma_{\mathcal A}$ mean ordinary right-derived sections at the terminal object, valued in $D^+(R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$.
For $M\in D^+(\mathcal D,R)$ the canonical comparison induced by $\Gamma_{\mathcal C}f_*\cong\Gamma_{\mathcal D}$ is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_{f,M}:R\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(Rf_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(M).$$
Put $T_f(K)=\lambda_{f,f^{-1}K}\circ R\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(\eta_{f,K})$, and similarly for $g$ and $fg$. These maps are natural in $K$. For the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism $c:g^{-1}f^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(fg)^{-1}$,
$$T_{fg}(K)=R\Gamma_{\mathcal E}(c_K)\circ T_g(f^{-1}K)\circ T_f(K).$$
If $h:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ is another geometric morphism and $\alpha:g^{-1}f^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}$ is induced by a geometric $2$-isomorphism $h\cong fg$, then
$$T_h(K)=R\Gamma_{\mathcal E}(\alpha_K)\circ T_g(f^{-1}K)\circ T_f(K).$$
Here the $2$-isomorphism is on sheaves of sets and induces the constant-$R$ module comparison; an arbitrary $R$-linear automorphism of a module inverse image is not allowed. For a sheaf $K$ in degree zero, $H^q(T_f(K))$ is the usual cohomology pullback: choose injective resolutions $K\to I^\bullet$ and $f^{-1}K\to J^\bullet$, apply sections to the ordinary section pullback into $f^{-1}I^\bullet$ and to any comparison $f^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ over $f^{-1}K$, and take cohomology. This holds for every integer $q$, with zero groups for $q<0$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal M_{\mathcal A}=\Mod(\underline R_{\mathcal A})$ and let $Q$ denote complex localization in the appropriate category. These are Grothendieck abelian categories by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Use degreewise monomorphic, bounded-below injective replacements $A\to I$ from [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono]. They are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Localization on maps into them is bijective by [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison]. Thus derived objects and morphisms may be computed on these replacements, with chain maps unique up to homotopy. The section functors are additive and left exact: kernels and finite products of module sheaves are evaluated sectionwise. Denote their right-derived comparisons by $\beta_{\mathcal A,P}:Q\Gamma_{\mathcal A}P\to R\Gamma_{\mathcal A}(QP)$, and the comparison for $u_*$ by $a_{u,P}:Q(u_*P)\to Ru_*(QP)$. They are natural, and invertible on bounded-below injective complexes, by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective].

proof.text: Let $1_{\mathcal A}$ denote the terminal sheaf. Global sections of a set sheaf $F$ are maps $1_{\mathcal A}\to F$. Since $u^{-1}1_{\mathcal A}\cong1_{\mathcal B}$, the adjunction of [def-trf-geometric-morphism] gives a natural bijection $s_{u,F}:\Gamma_{\mathcal A}(u_*F)\cong\Gamma_{\mathcal B}F$. Applied to the underlying module sheaf it is $R$-linear: addition is induced by the product map $F\times F\to F$, and multiplication by $r\in R$ by the corresponding endomorphism of $F$; naturality of the adjunction bijection respects both. Coefficient identifications preserve these constant scalars by hypothesis. Define $p_{u,F}=s_{u,u^{-1}F}\Gamma_{\mathcal A}(\eta^0_{u,F})$. Its value on a section $x:1_{\mathcal A}\to F$ is precisely $u^{-1}(x):1_{\mathcal B}\to u^{-1}F$, since the adjunct of $\eta^0_{u,F}x$ is $\varepsilon_{u,u^{-1}F}u^{-1}(\eta^0_{u,F})u^{-1}(x)=u^{-1}(x)$ by the triangle identity. These constructions apply degreewise to complexes and commute with differentials by naturality.

source.place: Tag 00XA, definition-topos; adjunction and terminal-object definition of global sections

proof.text: The preceding description proves the underived identities directly. For a module map $v:F\to F'$, $u^{-1}(v)u^{-1}(x)=u^{-1}(vx)$ gives $\Gamma_{\mathcal B}(u^{-1}v)p_{u,F}=p_{u,F'}\Gamma_{\mathcal A}(v)$. For a section $x:1_{\mathcal C}\to F$, naturality of the canonical compositor gives $c_Fg^{-1}f^{-1}(x)=(fg)^{-1}(x)c_1$; its component $c_1$ is the unique map between the two terminal sheaves. Hence $p_{fg,F}=\Gamma_{\mathcal E}(c_F)p_{g,f^{-1}F}p_{f,F}$. The same calculation for the inverse-image isomorphism $\alpha$ of the given geometric $2$-isomorphism yields $p_{h,F}=\Gamma_{\mathcal E}(\alpha_F)p_{g,f^{-1}F}p_{f,F}$. Here $\alpha_1$ is again the unique terminal comparison because $\alpha$ is defined on sheaves of sets [def-trf-geometric-morphism]; its induced module comparison has this same underlying map. This proves these equalities as $R$-linear maps, degreewise for complexes. It explains exactly why an arbitrary module automorphism cannot be substituted for $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 04IA, definition-2-morphism-topoi and its mate description; terminal-component naturality

proof.text:
For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $\mathcal D$, $f_*I$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives on $\mathcal C$: apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to the stipulated exact $f^{-1}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] computes both $R\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(Rf_*QI)$ and $R\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(QI)$ by $\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(f_*I)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathcal D}I$. Define $\lambda_{f,QI}$ by $Q(s_{f,I})$ under these identifications. Its naturality on chain maps and homotopies gives naturality on derived morphisms, using the K-injective localization bijection of Step 1. This is the canonical comparison induced by $s_f$, not just some isomorphism. More explicitly, for any bounded-below complex $P$ it satisfies
$$\lambda_{f,QP}\,R\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(a_{f,P})\,\beta_{\mathcal C,f_*P}=\beta_{\mathcal D,P}\,Q(s_{f,P}).\tag{*}$$
To verify $(*)$, choose $r:P\to I$. The comparison $a_{f,P}$, followed by $Rf_*(Qr)$ and identified on $I$, is $Q(f_*r)$ by naturality of $a_f$. Naturality of $\beta_{\mathcal C}$ converts the left side into sections of $f_*r$ followed by $s_{f,I}$. The equation $s_{f,I}\Gamma_{\mathcal C}(f_*r)=\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(r)s_{f,P}$ and naturality of $\beta_{\mathcal D}$ give the right side; cancel the invertible $Qr$ identifications. This also specifies the normalization on every complex.

source.place: Tag 08J6, remark-before-Leray; derived.tex Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors, injective model

proof.text:
Represent $K$ on $\mathcal C$ by a bounded-below injective complex $I$. Exactness identifies $f^{-1}K$ with $Q(f^{-1}I)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Choose a monomorphic injective replacement $b:f^{-1}I\to J$ using [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono]. The unit equation of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction], with the exact-localization identifications understood, reads $\eta_{f,QI}=a_{f,f^{-1}I}Q(\eta^0_{f,I})$. Apply $R\Gamma_{\mathcal C}$ and then $(*)$. Naturality of $\beta_{\mathcal C}$ gives
$$T_f(QI)\,\beta_{\mathcal C,I}=\beta_{\mathcal D,f^{-1}I}\,Q(p_{f,I}).$$
After the replacement $b$, this says that $T_f(K)$ is represented by the actual chain map
$$\Gamma_{\mathcal C}I\xrightarrow{p_{f,I}}\Gamma_{\mathcal D}(f^{-1}I)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_{\mathcal D}b}\Gamma_{\mathcal D}J.\tag{**}$$
The middle complex is not asserted to compute derived sections; its map to derived sections is $\beta_{\mathcal D,f^{-1}I}$, and naturality along $b$ justifies the replacement. Thus no preservation of injectives by $f^{-1}$ is used. Naturality of $T_f$ follows already from its definition as the composite of the natural unit, $R\Gamma$, and $\lambda_f$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; Tag 013K; canonical derived unit as in read-only PlusAdjunction.lean, derivedPlus_unit_app_fac lines 143–149

proof.text:
Retain $I,b,J$ from Step 5 and choose a monomorphic injective replacement $d:g^{-1}J\to H$. Exactness of $g^{-1}$ makes $d\,g^{-1}(b):g^{-1}f^{-1}I\to H$ a quasi-isomorphism and a degreewise monomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. It therefore also computes the composite pullback target; for $(fg)^{-1}I$ use $d\,g^{-1}(b)c_I^{-1}$. Apply $(**)$ twice. The chain map representing $T_g(f^{-1}K)T_f(K)$ is
$$\Gamma d\,p_{g,J}\,\Gamma b\,p_{f,I}=\Gamma(d\,g^{-1}b)\,p_{g,f^{-1}I}\,p_{f,I},$$
where the equality is precisely naturality of $p_g$ from Step 3. The model for $T_{fg}(K)$ is
$$\Gamma(d\,g^{-1}b c_I^{-1})\,p_{fg,I}=\Gamma(d\,g^{-1}b)\,p_{g,f^{-1}I}\,p_{f,I}.$$
The two target identifications differ by $R\Gamma_{\mathcal E}(c_K)$, so these equations prove exactly the required composition formula, in the derived category, before taking cohomology. Homotopy invariance makes the calculation independent of the displayed replacements.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist; sites.tex Tag 04IA; agent assembly of the chain-map identities in Steps 3 and 5

proof.text:
Set $L=(fg)^{-1}$ and $\delta=\alpha c^{-1}:L\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}$. For a replacement $r:LI\to V$, use $r\delta_I^{-1}:h^{-1}I\to V$ as the replacement on the $h$ side. Step 3 gives $p_{h,I}=\Gamma(\delta_I)p_{fg,I}$, so the two chain models from $(**)$ agree after identifying their targets:
$$\Gamma(r\delta_I^{-1})p_{h,I}=\Gamma(r)p_{fg,I}.$$
Termwise $\delta$ represents its derived isomorphism because both inverse images are exact [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] (equivalently apply the defining universal property of localization to its components). Consequently $T_h(K)=R\Gamma_{\mathcal E}(\delta_K)T_{fg}(K)$. Substitute Step 6 and $\delta c=\alpha$ to obtain the stated formula with $\alpha$. This uses the geometric terminal-component equation of Step 3; it asserts no corresponding invariance for arbitrary $R$-linear automorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04IA, definition-2-morphism-topoi; induced inverse-image mate and terminal-component naturality

proof.text: Finally let $K$ be a sheaf in degree zero. Choose $K\to I$ and $f^{-1}K\to J$ with no negative terms. The map $f^{-1}K\to f^{-1}I$ is a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism by exactness, and [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] supplies a chain map $b:f^{-1}I\to J$ over $f^{-1}K$. It is a quasi-isomorphism since both augmentations are. The same unit and comparison calculation proving $(**)$ applies to this $b$, so its section chain map is exactly the one in the statement. Any two choices of $b$ are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy], applied to $f^{-1}K\to f^{-1}I$ and the injective target $J$. Applying the additive section functor preserves a chain homotopy degreewise. Thus every allowed comparison yields $H^q(T_f(K))$ and the usual resolution-defined pullback. For $q<0$ the section complexes have zero terms, and therefore zero cohomology. This proves the assertion for every integer $q$.
